assignments.raw_value: Temporary courtesy licenses may be issued to nonresidents; military members and spouses may receive temporary courtesy licenses if they hold a current license in another state with substantially equivalent requirements.
Licensee may verify license with a reciprocating state for fees not greater than $75 as set by the board.

The board may develop reciprocal agreements with other states with similar licensing responsibilities. Under general umbrella law, occupational licensing entities must adopt least restrictive requirements for individuals holding substantially similar licenses from other states.

Reciprocity available if the other state accepts CA qualifications and has professional qualifications and conditions of good standing at least equal to CA; trade examination may be waived if applicant provides written certification of good standing for previous five years.

A county must issue a license to a building contractor holding a valid license from another county or municipality in Colorado, without requiring an additional exam, if the original license required passing a nationally recognized ICC exam. The fee charged by the secondary county is limited to processing costs.
Applicant must hold a similar license from a state with substantially similar or higher requirements, and that state must grant reciprocal licensure to CT licensees without examination.

Applicant must meet one of: (a) passed substantially equivalent exam and met FL requirements; (b) holds valid license from another state with substantially equivalent criteria; (c) holds valid license from state with reciprocal agreement; or (d) held valid license for at least 10 years before application. Division I contractors and roofing contractors must complete a 2-hour course on the Florida Building Code.

Other state must have substantially equivalent requirements; applicant must hold a current valid license from that state; criteria for that state's license must have been substantially equivalent to Georgia's; application materials and exam results must be available for review; applicant must demonstrate Georgia qualifications and comply with all Georgia requirements; similar privilege must be offered to Georgia residents by the other state.

Emergency licensure by endorsement available during declared state of emergency/disaster when board determines shortage of HI licensed contractors exists; applicant must show current out-of-state license in good standing for 2 years, provide proof of liability/property damage insurance, workers' compensation insurance, a financial statement, applicable fees, state tax clearance, and bond.

Must be currently licensed in another jurisdiction with substantially similar scope of practice, license in good standing, met minimum educational and experience requirements in issuing jurisdiction, passed required exams, no revocations or discipline, no pending complaints, pay applicable fees, no disqualifying criminal history.

Applicant must provide a verified copy of a current and unrestricted license, registration, or certification from a local government entity (pre-January 1, 2007 ordinance), pay a reciprocal registration fee not to exceed $50, and the prior credential must have been granted under provisions not less stringent than those of this chapter.

Applicant must hold a valid license from a state with substantially equal or greater requirements that grants reciprocal privileges to KY licensees; terms and conditions promulgated by administrative regulation.

The board may waive the trade portion of the examination for applicants holding a comparable license in another state, upon written certification that the applicant passed the examination and is in good standing. The business law requirement shall not be waived. Applicants must comply with all other licensing requirements; the board may waive other requirements for good cause.
Nonresident must conform with the article, file an irrevocable consent to service of process, and (if a corporation) be authorized to do business in Michigan.

Applicant must hold a current and valid license in another state in an occupation with similar scope of practice for at least one year, meet minimum education/experience/examination requirements verified by the other state, have no disqualifying criminal record, not have surrendered a license for negligence or misconduct, have no pending complaints, and pay all applicable fees.
To the extent other states provide for licensing of general contractors and provide for similar reciprocal action; applicant must show qualifications equal to NC licensees and pay the required fee.

Out-of-state licensee must have actively used the license for 2 of the past 3 years, demonstrate competency, have no disqualifying acts or discipline in the last 10 years, not be under active investigation, and pay applicable fees.

Experience obtained under a contractor in another state with substantially equivalent requirements, or as a contractor in another state with substantially equivalent requirements, may count toward the two-year experience requirement.

Reciprocal agreement with another state having equivalent licensing requirements; also expedited licensure available for military service members and veterans with substantially equivalent out-of-state credentials.

Applicant must hold a valid and unrestricted corresponding license in another state/territory, possess substantially similar qualifications, have no disciplinary history, pay applicable fees, submit fingerprints, and submit required statements.

A written reciprocity agreement between Ohio and the other state must exist; the other state's requirements must be substantially equal to Ohio's; the other state must extend similar reciprocity to Ohio licensees; the applicant must pay the Ohio licensure fee.

The Board may rely upon proof of a valid construction license or registration issued by another state to expedite processing; insurance and workers' compensation requirements must demonstrate compliance for work in this state.

Reciprocal licensing available when other state's standards, qualifications and examinations are substantially similar to Oregon's; issued without examination upon proof of out-of-state licensing and payment of appropriate fees.
Available for military members and spouses relocating to RI pursuant to military orders, where the other state's requirements are substantially equivalent to RI's requirements.

Applicant must hold a license or certificate in good standing in another state with requirements equal to or greater than South Carolina's; exam waiver agreement must be authorized by the board. Applicant may also exempt the technical exam by verifying passage of an essentially equivalent exam in another state, even without a reciprocal agreement. Must pass the SC Commercial Contractors Business, Law and Project Management exam and comply with all other licensing and certification requirements.

Reciprocity is recognized for contractors from states that practice reciprocity with Tennessee. Applicants from non-reciprocal states must apply with an affidavit stating they have not performed contracting work in TN exceeding $2,500. Masonry contractors must always take and pass the masonry examination regardless of reciprocity.

License by endorsement available under 58-1-302: similar scope of practice, at least 1 year of experience, license in good standing in other state. Division may also evaluate applicants not meeting these criteria for substantial similarity of education/experience.

Applicant must hold a current and valid license in another state in a profession with similar scope of practice, held for at least 3 years; other state required exam and education/training/experience standards; no pending investigations; good standing; no disqualifying criminal record; no discipline (except financial-only); pay applicable fees.

The education, experience, and examination requirements in the other state must be at least equivalent to Wisconsin requirements. Individual must submit application, pay fee, and hold a valid comparable credential from the other state.

Reciprocity available to the extent other states provide similar action; applicant must show qualifications equal to WV licensees, pay required fee, and provide certification as required by §30-42-15(c).

License must be active and contractor must be in good standing with the issuing jurisdiction; must provide proof of exam completion (ICC or equivalent); must provide any required proof of financial assurance to the accepting jurisdiction; accepting jurisdiction may deny recognition if contractor previously had a license revoked or suspended by that jurisdiction.
